title: Paper
description: Paper, in paper look cinematography, is the world as pulp: torn stock, visible fibers, a person as a cut-out on a page. The world is pulp, and creased lawful sculpture is origami, not this.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Titles, stop-motion paper, a figure that has been scissored from stock: hard or window light that shows the edge of the sheet, fibers in the tear. Collage stacks pieces.
Paper is the material of the whole world. It is the wrong tool when the paper is neatly folded into facets, and the wrong tool when the person is simply standing in a library.
Show the cut and the fiber.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Paper in film?
A pulp-material look: torn stock, visible fibers, a person as a cut-out. The world is the sheet, not a prop in a hand.
Paper vs Origami
Paper is tear and fiber. Origami is crease and facet. If the world folds on lawful lines, you wanted origami.
When should I use Paper?
Titles, cut-out worlds, pulp as set. Skip neat folds and library portraits with a book as a prop.
How do I prompt Paper for AI image or video?
Raking light, then: Paper world of [Subject], torn stock, visible fibers, a person as a cut-out on pulp. Demand fibers and a tear. Forbid origami creases.
